title: A Orbit for the Colony
premise: Rosalind Okonkwo smuggles memories through orbital customs aboard her patched freighter, the only lifeline between the forgotten colony of Meridian and the rest of humanity. When the colony's children begin sharing a single dream — a message encoded in their minds by a dying terraforming AI — Rosalind realizes the dream contains proof that the colonial fleet's war was manufactured by the very admiralty now negotiating a truce. As customs agents close in and the truce clock runs down, she must choose between selling the memory for her own freedom or broadcasting it and becoming the enemy of both sides. She broadcasts it, igniting a reckoning that ends the war but costs her ship, her anonymity, and nearly her life — leaving Meridian visible at last, and Rosalind its unwilling witness.
about_author: Rosalind Hartwell is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to ships that never came home, an obsession that bleeds into her fiction. She writes from a coastal town where the fog does most of the talking.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs introduces Rosalind's world: black-market memory chips hidden in engine coolant, bribed inspectors, and the fading colony below that no one official remembers exists. The emotional beat is weary competence masking loneliness — she's good at being invisible, and it's starting to feel like disappearing.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: POV: Amara, a twelve-year-old teacher's aide on Meridian. Forty-three children wake from the same dream: a tower of light speaking in a voice none of them know. Their parents dismiss it; Amara records it. The beat is uncanny wonder curdling into fear as the adults' refusal to listen mirrors how the whole colony has been ignored.

chapters.title: Cargo That Screams
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. A client pays triple for an unmarked chip, but when Rosalind previews it to verify contents, she finds a fragment of the same dream — recorded from an adult who died years ago. Someone has been harvesting this before. The beat is dread: her safe, transactional world just became personal.

chapters.title: The Admiralty's Quiet War
chapters.summary: POV: Inspector Dae-Ho Voss, customs officer with debts and ambitions. He traces the anomalous memory traffic back toward Meridian and discovers fleet records listing the colony as 'decommissioned' — though ten thousand people still live there. The beat is moral vertigo as Voss realizes his career is built on paperwork that erases the living.

chapters.title: What the Terraformer Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind, descending to Meridian. Following the dream's coordinates, she finds the buried terraforming AI, half-mad after decades alone, which reveals it seeded the dream into the children because only unregistered minds escape fleet surveillance. It holds the admiral's original order falsifying the war's cause. The beat is terrible inheritance: truth passed to those too young to carry it.

chapters.title: Truce Expiration
chapters.summary: POV: Multiple, braided. The fleet announces a 72-hour truce extension for final negotiations; Voss files his report and is ordered to bury it. On Meridian, officials try to quarantine the dreaming children, and Amara leads them into the tunnels. The beat is accelerating panic — every institution chooses self-preservation over truth.

chapters.title: The Price of Visibility
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind. Voss corners her at dockside with an offer: hand over the AI's memory and he'll look away. Instead she copies it to him and keeps the original, gambling that a man who erases people for a living might want to stop. The beat is fragile trust — two smugglers of different kinds betting everything on each other.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Amara and Rosalind, alternating. With customs lockdown sealing the port, the children use the dream-link itself as a carrier wave while Rosalind hijacks the orbital relay to transmit the admiral's confession fleet-wide. Voss stalls the inspection long enough to matter. The beat is defiant climax — the invisible made unbearably loud.

chapters.title: The War That Ends Ugly
chapters.summary: POV: Voss. The broadcast shatters negotiations; mutinies spread through both fleets as soldiers learn the war was purchased. The admiralty falls, but not cleanly — reprisals, arrests, a bombardment narrowly averted when crews refuse orders. The beat is bitter victory: justice arrives, wearing blood, outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: An Orbit for the Colony
chapters.summary: POV: Rosalind, epilogue. Months later, Meridian has representation, supply lines, and its name back on the charts. Rosalind, shipless and famous against her will, takes a teaching post beside Amara, who still dreams — but now only ordinary dreams. The beat is quiet restoration: visibility as belonging, not exposure, and memory finally kept honestly.
